page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-16 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated physical processor cores running on the Intel Xeon 6354 platform at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. Utilizing symmetric multiprocessing with two hardware threads per core, the configuration exposes 8 virtual central processing units alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a tight 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual processor.

Hardware accelerators are absent in this shape, with zero physical GPUs provisioned. Local storage is also designated as none, requiring external block storage volumes for system and runtime persistence. Networking includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address for ingress and egress routing. Because all compute units are dedicated rather than shared or burstable, compute execution avoids multi-tenant resource contention.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio prioritizes core density over capacity, aligning resource costs directly with processing-bound operations. This layout reduces memory overhead expenses for computational tasks that do not consume large in-memory caches. Tradeoffs include reliance on networked storage protocols for all I/O transactions and operational limits for memory-intensive data structures.

The VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-16 profile fits compute-centric workloads including continuous integration pipelines, batch job execution, microservice computation, and application server hosting requiring consistent per-core clock frequencies.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-16 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured for compute-oriented application workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated physical cores supporting 8 vCPUs via two execution threads per core. System allocation includes 16.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a lean 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. The platform integrates zero graphics processing units and excludes local storage disks, relying on remote network volumes for disk access, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. With fully dedicated processor allocation, CPU execution avoids noisy-neighbor throttling typical of burstable instances. This technical architecture suits CPU-focused batch processing, web serving layers, continuous integration workers, and lightweight computational services.
